question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.**

I will driving/you to/the station/ in the morning.
solution:
The correct answer is: "**I will driving**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error in the sentence is the use of "**will driving**," which is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The verb "**will**" indicates the future tense.
 
• When we use "will" to express a future action, we typically follow it with the base form of the verb (infinitive form).
 
• In this case, the correct form of the verb to use after "will" is "**drive**," which is the base form (**infinitive**) of the verb.
 
• **The correct sentence would be** *"I will drive you to the station in the morning."*
 
• In this corrected sentence, we have the future tense "**will drive**," which is the grammatically accurate way to express that you will be the one driving to the station in the morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.
